messages:
eli: Hey — noticing weird behavior in the us-west1 GPU pool. Overall reported utilization ~80% but several nodes show 0% usage while queue is ballooning to 400+. Looks like head-of-line blocking from a large batch job (batch-712).

maya: Which scheduler are you hitting (new placement scoring or legacy)?

eli: New placement scoring (merged last week). Job batch-712 reserved 16 GPUs but is only pulling tokens for 4, and admission control isn't letting smaller jobs bypass it. Queue length per pool: 420. Backpressure triggers firing.

sre-bot: Alert: queue_depth(us-west1-gpu) = 420 at 2026-03-15T10:12:13Z. Slow-schedule-events++

sam: That rings a bell — PR #3581 changed the NodeAllocator snapshot logic to reduce contention. Might have introduced stale free_gpus reads.

rachael: If that's true, it would explain head-of-line blocking: scheduler picks the big job because the cached snapshot reports enough resources, but allocations fail and we never re-evaluate the queue head.

eli: Pasted scheduler log excerpt:
```
scheduler: placing job batch-712
node-snapshot.version=214
score(node-a)=0.94 score(node-b)=0.07
allocate(node-a, batch-712) -> allocated 4/16 gpus
post_alloc: snapshot still reports node-a free_gpus=12
```
This shows stale snapshot after allocation.

maya: Ugh. The cache isn't invalidated on allocate. PR 3581 replaced atomic reads with a cheaper snapshot but forgot to invalidate.

sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) enable preemption for low-priority jobs to free space, 2) temporarily disable snapshot caching (invalidate_on_alloc=true), or 3) adjust admission control to check live capacity before dequeue.

rachael: I can push a sched-config hotfix for (2) and flip admission control to probe live nodes for the next 60s. Also recommend lowering batch-712 max_gpus to 8 as a stopgap.

eli: Can we do hotswap? We need something up quickly — 10+ customers are seeing increased latency.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline started: sched-config-hotfix -> us-west1 canary (3 nodes)

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: sched-config-hotfix -> us-west1 (canary 3/10 nodes) at 1765001298

eli: Hotfix applied to canary: set snapshot.invalidate_on_alloc=true and admission_probe=60s. Observability: queue dropped 420 -> 95 within ~3 minutes, idle nodes decreased from 9 to 2.

maya: Nice. We should still revert the caching change in mainline and add unit + integration tests that simulate head-of-line blocking with stale snapshots.

sam: I'll open a follow-up: ISSUE-4821, assign to infra-scheduler, include regression test harness (synthetic jobs to validate preemption/backfill and snapshot invalidation).

rachael: Also let's add a metric: head_of_line_block_time{pool} and an alert if > 2m. That will catch regressions earlier.

eli: Agreed. Thanks for the quick turnaround. Leaving thread open until we ship the revert and tests. :thumbsup:
